query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor amount of boron (~0.5 at%) to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will improve its load-bearing integrity by enhancing grain boundary cohesion while preserving its large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy that exhibits excellent caloric performance but has poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Introduce approximately 0.5 at% boron via conventional arc-melting followed by homogenization annealing.
generation.conditions: Samples are processed and tested under the same caloric operating regimes—applied magnetic field and pressure-field—near the transition temperature and under mechanical loads representative of service conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron atoms are expected to segregate to the grain boundaries, thereby enhancing the cohesion between grains.
generation.mechanism: The boron doping improves grain boundary strength by reducing intergranular defects and inhibiting crack initiation and propagation. This is achieved without significantly interfering with the phase transformation mechanisms responsible for the caloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: The boron-doped alloy will exhibit a higher fracture toughness and improved resistance to cracking, while its caloric response (e.g., entropy and temperature changes under applied fields) remains comparable to that of the undoped alloy.
generation.baseline: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy shows high caloric performance under applied fields but suffers from poor mechanical integrity and cracking.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to the operational boundaries of the caloric device: under magnetic and pressure fields near the caloric transition temperature and under mechanical loading conditions typical of service.
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanism of boron-induced grain boundary strengthening is well established, the precise quantitative impact on the caloric performance remains uncertain. Minor compositional changes could potentially alter the caloric properties, but significant degradation is not expected.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 samples: one set undoped (control) and one set doped with ~0.5 at% boron. Process both sets by arc-melting and homogenization annealing under identical conditions. Then, subject the samples to identical tests including mechanical loading (e.g., fracture toughness measurements, tensile/compression tests) and caloric performance evaluations (calorimetry tests under applied magnetic and pressure fields near the caloric transition temperature).
measurements: Microstructural analysis (SEM/TEM) to confirm boron segregation at grain boundaries
Fracture toughness and strength tests to assess improvements in load-bearing integrity
Caloric effect measurements (e.g., temperature and entropy changes under applied fields)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the boron-doped samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in mechanical integrity (e.g., enhanced fracture toughness or delayed crack propagation) compared to the undoped samples, or if they exhibit a significant reduction or alteration in the caloric response under the applied magnetic or pressure fields.

cited_evidence.text: While the yield strength and KJIc fracture toughness of the medium-entropy CrCoNi and high-entropy CrMnFeCoNi alloys are comparable, the tensile strengths, tensile ductility and work of fracture of the CrCoNi alloy are significantly higher, by respectively ∼15, ∼30 and ∼50%, at room temperature. At cryogenic temperatures, the strengths of the two alloys are comparable (σUTS∼1,300 MPa at 77 K), but the KJIc fracture toughness, tensile ductility and work of fracture are again markedly higher in the CrCoNi alloy, by ∼25, ∼27 and ∼31%, respectively. The yield strength, σy, at 77 K is slightly below that of the CrMnFeCoNi alloy, which we believe is due to the non-uniform grain size of our present material (Fig. 1b–d). Consistent with this notion, in a previous study where the grain size of CrCoNi was uniform and comparable to that of the CrMnFeCoNi alloy, the tensile properties of the three-component alloy were found to exceed those of the five-component alloy at all temperatures.

chosen.lever: minor alloying addition (introducing ~0.5 at% boron) to improve grain boundary cohesion
chosen.technique: standard alloying via arc-melting and homogenization annealing, followed by microstructural (e.g., SEM, TEM) and mechanical (e.g., fracture toughness, compression tests) evaluations
chosen.conditions: The intervention is performed such that the alloy is processed under the same magnetic field and pressure regimes (typical for caloric refrigeration) and tested at temperatures close to the caloric transition, under mechanical loads representative of service conditions
chosen.why: This approach directly addresses the niche by targeting the poor load-bearing integrity through a well-established composition change method.
